note: Which SUBSTRATE each gauntlet campaign's transactions actually ran on. `bindings.json` says a campaign drove a route; it does not say whether the thing that executed the route was Solana devnet, a `solana-test-validator`, or an in-process `solana-program-test` bank. Those are three different evidence levels (AGENTS.md, 'Correctness vocabulary'; tools/gauntlet/DESIGN.md admits ProgramTest only as a labelled fast lane) and until this file existed the register could not print the difference, so 53% of the witnessed rows read exactly like the 19 that reach a validator. One file, one owner (lane WITNESS), because a substrate declared inside each campaign's own bindings.json would be the campaign grading its own evidence. Every declaration here is CHECKED against its producer by tools/genref/generate.mjs: `local-validator` must NAME `solana-test-validator` in executable text -- in the runner, or in a script the runner invokes, with shell comments stripped first -- `program-test` must not, and a campaign with no row is a hard error rather than a silent `unknown`. That control was a text search over the raw runner file until 2026-09-04, and `lineage-loopback` passed it on a COMMENT in run-lineage.sh's header while its validator lived one level down in tools/lineage-loopback/run-lineage-loopback.sh -- a control that could not fail for the reason it exists. tools/genref/substrate-control.mjs is the check and states what it does and does not claim; tools/genref/test.sh proves it red on a synthetic comment-only runner. Each row also states whether the campaign REPRODUCES: `reproducible` is true, or a sentence saying what stops it. A binding is a claim about a run that happened, and a claim whose run cannot be repeated is not corroboration -- the C-16 rehearsal's finding (b), that 25 routes' sole witness was a campaign refusing at HEAD, was only findable by trying to run it. Now the register prints it.

classes.devnet: A finalized transaction on Solana devnet, named by signature and slot. The only class that is chain evidence outside this machine. Contract item 5 (docs/MASTER_COMPLETION_CONTRACT.md:52-53) is met by this or by `local-validator`.
classes.local-validator: A `solana-test-validator` process: a real Agave runtime, a real ledger, real slots and finalization, on localhost.
classes.program-test: An in-process `solana-program-test` bank. It executes REAL SBF ELFs, which is why these campaigns are evidence at all, but it is not a validator: no packet limit, no leader schedule, no finalization, and no fee market. A route whose only witness is this class has never been exercised by a runtime that could refuse it for size or for time.
classes.reproducible: Whether the campaign completes at HEAD. `true` means it was observed to run end to end; a sentence means it does not, and says where it stops. Not a claim that anyone ran it today: it is an authored field, and it goes stale the same way every authored field does. What it is for is that a campaign which STOPS reproducing has somewhere to say so, which it did not before.

DCLRLND1, the successor declaration, on a real Agave runtime with genesis-staged activation caches. THE RUN IS NOT NEW: `tools/lineage-loopback/run-lineage-loopback.sh` has been landing this transaction, reading the 248-byte record back off the chain and refusing a replay with `LineageAlreadyDeclared`, for as long as it has existed -- while `registry/lineage_v1::process` read NEVER-EXECUTED, because the run swept its own evidence away with the ledger and no campaign folded it. Third instance in two days of the same shape, a green driver with no producer (ABORT-WITNESS found the other two), and the smallest of the three: an `--evidence-dir` flag, a `transactions` array in the document the caller already wrote, and a bindings file. No program changed and the run does what it did before. What this substrate proves past `programs/dclutch-registry-sbf/tests/lineage_program_test.rs` is the CALLER's plumbing: the finalized multi-account read, the vacant-address mapping, the keyless simulation's wire format, the signer set, and the read-back that compares landed bytes against projected ones. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, and the runner's own header says so before anything else: that a real activation ladder produced these caches. They are composed offline and injected at genesis, which the route permits because it authenticates a cache's owner, width, decodability and derived address and asks nothing about provenance. Cut-day evidence comes from devnet's real caches; this campaign is not a substitute for it.
